text:
jen: Hey team — auditor (Amy) wants demonstrable proof of the RBAC approval flow for service-account changes, plus KMS decrypt/logs for any emergency key operations in the last 180 days. She also asked for evidence tying a recent vuln triage to the incident timeline.

sahil: Ack. Do we have one single playbook export that ties policy changes -> PR -> approvals -> deploy? :thinking_face:

maria: We have the 'rbac-change-playbook' runbook in Confluence, but auditors want an artifact bundle (signed approvals + log slices). I can produce the PR diffs and Github review history.

jen: Good — they explicitly asked for non-redacted logs showing KMS usage and the KMS key id(s). We should include: the KMS Decrypt API calls, the IAM principal that called it, and the session context/role.

maria: For logs, we can pull CloudTrail for the KMS region. Quick query I usually run:
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2025-08-01 --end-time 2026-02-28 --region us-west-2
```
That returns eventTime, userIdentity, and requestParameters.keyId.

jen: Perfect. Also include the matching CloudWatch log snapshots for the service that consumed the decrypted data (if available) so auditor can link usage to business purpose.

sahil: About RBAC change approvals, we need the chain: JIRA ticket -> PR -> 2 approvers -> changelog deploy tag. I can export the PR timeline with review comments and the GPG-signed merge commit.

maria: I'll compile: PR permalink, reviewer list, approval timestamps. Should we also include SSO login snapshots showing approver MFA events? Auditor asked for proof the approvers were who they said they were.

jen: Yes. Pull SSO login events for the approver accounts for the approval window. The query is in the evidence playbook — basically Okta/AzureAD auth logs for the approver UPN during the approval time.

auditor-amy: Thanks all. For the vulnerability triage piece, we need: the vulnerability ticket (internal ID), the initial detection time, the triage notes, and any follow-up remediation or mitigations. Also attach the CVE reference if applicable.

maria: The vuln ticket is SEC-4571. Detected 2026-01-12. We marked as P2, performed a compensating control (temp network ACL) and scheduled patching. Patch applied on 2026-01-20. I'll attach the triage notes.

jen: Make sure to export the timeline showing when the vuln was linked to the service account change (if it was). The auditor asked for linkage between configuration drift and the vulnerability window.

sahil: One thing — KMS logs only show API call metadata, not plaintext. Auditor asked for 'decrypt proof' to show key usage. We can provide the Decrypt event + the consumer's requestId and the downstream service log entry that consumed the decrypted blob and performed the operation. That should satisfy non-repudiation without exposing secrets.

maria: Agreed. I'll correlate requestId across CloudTrail (KMS) and the application logs (we have request_id in headers). If we can't link, we add a note saying linkage unavailable and why.

oncall-bot: Reminder: evidence exports may contain PII/secret material. Use secure artifact bucket (s3://redwood-evidence-enc) with SSE-KMS and pre-signed link for auditor. Expire links after 72h.

jen: Good reminder. Use the dedicated evidence bucket and attach a manifest listing all files + hash (sha256) for tamper-proofing. Include the bucket IAM policy and access logs.

auditor-amy: Also please include the control mapping: which SOC2 control(s) these artifacts satisfy (e.g., CC6.1 change management, CC7.2 key management). A short mapping table is fine.

maria: I'll draft a one-page control mapping: RBAC change artifacts -> CC6.1, PR approvals -> CC6.3, KMS Decrypt events -> CC7.1/7.2, Vulnerability triage notes -> CC5.1.

sahil: Timeline for delivery? I can have the PR + approvals export by EOD. Maria can do CloudTrail slices and manifests by tomorrow morning. Jen can assemble the mapping and the SSO proof.

jen: Sounds good. Maria — when you run the CloudTrail export, please include the raw event JSON (not just CSV) and redact any session tokens. Also include the filter command you used.

maria: Will do. Example CloudTrail filter I will save with the export:
```json
{"LookupAttributes": [{"AttributeKey": "EventName", "AttributeValue": "Decrypt"}], "StartTime": "2025-08-01T00:00:00Z", "EndTime": "2026-02-28T23:59:59Z"}
```

maria: One more Q — do we need to include KMS key rotation history? Auditor asked earlier about key rotation policy for the emergency key used.

jen: Yes include rotation status and key schedule. If the key is opted-out of automatic rotation (for HSM-backed or imported keys), include justification and compensating controls.

sahil: For the vuln linkage, I'll export the service deploy tags around 2026-01-10..2026-01-25 and the config diffs. That should show if a change correlated with the vuln window.

auditor-amy: Thanks. One last ask: can you produce a short demo (screen capture or step-by-step screenshots) showing the RBAC change approval flow and how a KMS decrypt event is found in CloudTrail? 5-7 screenshots is fine.

jen: We can record 3 screenshots + a short narrated mp4 (under 3 minutes). We'll upload to the evidence bucket.

maria: Plan: gather CloudTrail raw JSON, app logs with request_id, PR/approval artifacts, SSO login snapshots, KMS key metadata, key rotation policy, vulnerability ticket and remediation notes, control mapping, and demo screenshots. Bundle and upload to s3://redwood-evidence-enc/auditor-amy-2026-03-02/.

sahil: I'll add checksums and a README that lists each file and which control it maps to.

jen: Great. Assigning owners: PR+approvals -> sahil, CloudTrail/KMS slices -> maria, SSO snapshots + mapping doc -> jen, Demo -> maria.

auditor-amy: That's excellent. Can you confirm delivery ETA?

maria: ETA for bundle upload: 2026-03-03 10:00 UTC.

jen: We'll send presigned read-only link and short index email to you once uploaded.

auditor-amy: Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:
